title: Computer Networks
description: Computer Networks studies how independently administered, heterogeneous systems communicate reliably, efficiently, securely, and at global scale. Students move from signals, frames, addressing, forwarding, and routing to transport, congestion control, applications, wireless access, security, measurement, network programmability, and cloud/data-center design. A single conceptual and laboratory core serves all three degrees. Computer Engineering adds stronger link/forwarding and hardware-performance analysis, while MS Computer Science adds original-paper reading, algorithmic depth, experimental rigor, and a research-quality project extension.

topics.title: Network Architecture, Layering, and Internet Design Principles
topics.description: This opening unit gives students the mental model for how networks are organized. It explains why layered design makes a global Internet possible while still allowing technologies to evolve independently.

children.title: Layering models
children.description: Students learn how OSI and TCP/IP models divide networking responsibilities. The gist is to know what each layer abstracts from the layers above and below.

children.title: Internet design principles
children.description: Students learn the architectural ideas that shaped the Internet. These principles explain why intelligence often lives at the edge rather than inside the network core.

children.title: Protocols, services, and interfaces
children.description: Students learn the difference between what a layer provides and how it provides it.

children.title: Network types and topologies
children.description: Students learn common network scopes and shapes before studying specific technologies.

topics.title: Physical Layer, Data Transmission, and Performance Metrics
topics.description: This unit covers how bits move across media and how engineers reason about capacity, delay, and reliability. It grounds abstract protocols in physical constraints.

children.title: Transmission media
children.description: Students learn the tradeoffs among wired, wireless, and optical media. The point is to see that medium choice affects bandwidth, distance, interference, and cost.

children.title: Signals and encoding
children.description: Students learn how digital data is represented for transmission.

children.title: Performance metrics
children.description: Students learn the numbers used to describe network quality.

children.title: Delay and capacity calculations
children.description: Students learn to estimate where time is spent in a network path.

topics.title: Data Link Layer, Error Detection, MAC, Ethernet, and Switching
topics.description: This unit explains local delivery across a single link or LAN. Students learn how frames, addresses, switching, and error checks make shared local networks work.

children.title: Framing and link-layer services
children.description: Students learn how raw bits become frames with boundaries and metadata.

children.title: Error detection
children.description: Students learn how networks detect corrupted frames.

children.title: Medium access control
children.description: Students learn how devices share a communication medium without chaos.

children.title: Ethernet and switching
children.description: Students learn the dominant LAN technology and how switches forward frames.

topics.title: IP Addressing, Subnetting, and Network-Layer Design
topics.description: This unit explains how networks identify hosts and organize address space. Subnetting becomes the practical skill that connects protocol theory to real network design.

children.title: IPv4 addressing
children.description: Students learn the structure and purpose of IP addresses.

children.title: Subnetting
children.description: Students learn to divide address space into usable networks. The gist is to match address allocation to topology and growth needs.

children.title: IPv6
children.description: Students learn why IPv6 exists and how it changes addressing.

children.title: Network-layer design
children.description: Students learn how addressing decisions shape routing, security, and manageability.

topics.title: Routing Algorithms, Routing Protocols, and Interdomain Routing
topics.description: Routing determines the path packets take through interconnected networks. Students learn both the algorithms and the operational protocols that keep the Internet connected.

children.title: Forwarding versus routing
children.description: Students learn the difference between moving one packet and computing paths.

children.title: Routing algorithms
children.description: Students learn classic path-selection ideas.

children.title: Interior routing protocols
children.description: Students learn how routing works inside an organization or autonomous system.

children.title: Interdomain routing
children.description: Students learn why Internet routing is shaped by policy as well as path length.

topics.title: Transport Layer: UDP, TCP, Reliability, and Flow Control
topics.description: This unit explains end-to-end communication between processes. Students learn how transport protocols provide reliability, ordering, ports, and flow management above IP.

children.title: Transport services
children.description: Students learn what applications need from transport and why UDP and TCP make different tradeoffs.

children.title: UDP
children.description: Students learn why a simple transport protocol is useful when applications manage their own reliability or prioritize latency.

children.title: TCP reliability
children.description: Students learn how TCP turns unreliable IP delivery into a reliable byte stream.

children.title: TCP connection and flow control
children.description: Students learn how TCP starts, ends, and prevents receiver overload.

topics.title: Congestion Control, Quality of Service, and Network Performance
topics.description: This unit studies what happens when networks get busy. Students learn how protocols and operators manage scarce capacity and performance expectations.

children.title: Congestion control
children.description: Students learn how TCP adapts sending rate to network conditions.

children.title: Queueing and loss
children.description: Students learn how buffers help and hurt network performance.

children.title: Quality of service
children.description: Students learn how networks prioritize or reserve resources for traffic with special needs.

children.title: Measurement and benchmarking
children.description: Students learn how to evaluate real network behavior.

topics.title: Application-Layer Protocols: HTTP, DNS, SMTP, and Web Networking
topics.description: This unit connects network foundations to the applications students use every day. Students learn how application protocols structure requests, responses, names, and delivery.

children.title: HTTP and web protocols
children.description: Students learn how browsers and servers communicate.

children.title: DNS
children.description: Students learn how names become addresses.

children.title: Email and messaging protocols
children.description: Students learn how message delivery is standardized.

children.title: Content delivery and web performance
children.description: Students learn how modern web systems reduce latency and increase reliability.

children.title: Modern encrypted transports
children.description: Students examine how transport and application protocols evolve together to reduce latency, encrypt metadata, and resist ossification.

topics.title: Socket Programming, Client-Server Design, and Protocol Implementation
topics.description: This unit makes networking concrete through code. Students learn how applications use sockets to send and receive data across networks.

children.title: Socket API basics
children.description: Students learn the programming interface between applications and the transport layer.

children.title: Client-server design
children.description: Students learn how networked applications organize roles and state.

children.title: Protocol parsing
children.description: Students learn to implement and debug message formats.

children.title: Testing network programs
children.description: Students learn practical ways to validate behavior.

topics.title: Wireless, Mobile, and Access Networks
topics.description: This unit examines networks where the medium is shared, mobile, and variable. Students learn why wireless networking has different constraints from wired Ethernet.

children.title: Wi-Fi fundamentals
children.description: Students learn the basic operation of 802.11 networks.

children.title: Cellular and mobile networking
children.description: Students learn how mobility changes addressing, handoff, and performance.

children.title: Wireless performance
children.description: Students learn why signal conditions and contention affect throughput.

children.title: Wireless security
children.description: Students learn baseline protections and common risks.

topics.title: Network Security: TLS, Firewalls, VPNs, Segmentation, and Zero Trust
topics.description: This unit introduces security as a design requirement, not an afterthought. Students learn how protocols and network architecture reduce risk.

children.title: Secure channels
children.description: Students learn how cryptography protects traffic in transit.

children.title: Perimeter and packet controls
children.description: Students learn how networks filter and control traffic.

children.title: VPNs and tunneling
children.description: Students learn how private communication is carried over shared networks.

children.title: Segmentation and zero trust
children.description: Students learn modern access-control ideas for limiting blast radius.

topics.title: Packet Analysis, Troubleshooting, and Network Operations
topics.description: This unit develops operational skill. Students learn to observe network behavior directly, diagnose failures, and manage networks as living systems.

children.title: Packet capture
children.description: Students learn to inspect traffic and connect packets to protocol theory.

children.title: Troubleshooting workflow
children.description: Students learn a systematic process for finding network problems.

children.title: Monitoring and logging
children.description: Students learn how operators maintain visibility.

children.title: Incident and alert context
children.description: Students learn the bridge from troubleshooting to defense.

topics.title: Software-Defined Networking, NFV, Data-Center, and Cloud Networking
topics.description: This unit covers modern network infrastructure. Students learn how control, forwarding, virtualization, and cloud platforms change network design.

children.title: Software-defined networking
children.description: Students learn how SDN separates control logic from forwarding devices.

children.title: Network function virtualization
children.description: Students learn how network services can run as software rather than dedicated appliances.

children.title: Data-center networking
children.description: Students learn the design pressures of large-scale server networks.

children.title: Cloud networking
children.description: Students learn the basic networking abstractions used by cloud platforms.

children.title: Programmable data planes
children.description: Students learn how modern switches expose packet parsing and match-action behavior to software, enabling faster experimentation and specialized forwarding.

topics.title: Emerging Networking Trends and Applied Network Design
topics.description: The final unit synthesizes the course into design judgment. Students connect protocols, security, performance, and operations to realistic network architecture choices.

children.title: Network design process
children.description: Students learn to turn requirements into an architecture.

children.title: Modern protocol trends
children.description: Students learn how protocols continue to evolve.

children.title: Edge and IoT networking
children.description: Students learn why constrained and distributed devices create new networking challenges.

children.title: Capstone-style design review
children.description: Students practice explaining and defending design choices.

children.title: Networking research and reproducible experimentation
children.description: Students learn how networking knowledge is created and challenged through standards, original papers, controlled experiments, and artifacts that others can inspect and rerun.

children.title: Reading RFCs and original research papers
Reproducible code, configuration, seeds, and raw data
Limitations, ethics, privacy, and responsible disclosure
